cards.front: What should you know about three-dimensional design exam tips?
cards.back: Produce drawings at a STATED SCALE (e.g. 1:50). Show at least PLAN and ELEVATION. Build a physical MODEL — photograph it. Explain how your design responds to its SPECIFIC site. Consider human scale — annotate dimensions.

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: Architectural design is just about drawing nice-looking buildings. Correct: Architectural design must address FUNCTION (how spaces are used), STRUCTURE (how the building stands up), CONTEXT (how it responds to its site and community), SUSTAINABILITY (energy efficiency, materials) and ATMOSPHERE (how it feels to be there) — not just appearance.

Design a small space (e.g. a pavilion, studio or room) for a specific site and purpose. Show plans, elevations, a scale model and a written rationale explaining how your design responds to its context.

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: Architectural and Interior Design
